newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. debt volatilities mixed.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. debt volatilities mixed.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. fixed income options were mixed in choppy late trading, shedding some of the early gains as underlying markets briefly popped off lows, dealers said.

Traders said volatilities softened somewhat after a mild, brief rally in futures on a newswire report that Dallas Federal Reserve Bank president Robert Mcteer said the Fed was not ready to tighten credit yet.
"It's been all over the place, but the net change is very small," said a brokerage trader at the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT).
Implied volatilities for CBOT April and June T-bond futures options were little changed from Monday's closes at around 9.0 and 9.5 percent respectively.
June T-bond futures, which earlier grinded down to a 109-20/32 low, clawed back up into positive territory on the McTeer comments in mid-afternoon.

But the rally was short-lived and the contract soon drifted back into negative territory as the market remained very cautious ahead of the March 25 Federal Open Market Committee meeting, traders said.
